recipes.name: Kristen’s Parmesan Roasted Potatoes
ingredients_raw: 1.5 pounds unpeeled potatoes, cut into 1-inch chunks

steps.text: Preheat an oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C).
Place potatoes into a mixing bowl and drizzle with olive oil. Sprinkle with kosher salt, black pepper, Parmesan cheese, and thyme leaves. Toss to evenly coat, and transfer to a 9x13-inch baking dish.
Bake in the preheated oven until potatoes are golden brown on the edges and tender when pierced with a fork, about 1 hour. Serve hot or at room temperature.

raw_recipe.headline: Kristen’s Parmesan Roasted Potatoes
raw_recipe.description: These roasted potatoes are coated in a Parmesan and thyme mixture. They are an easy side dish — just throw them in the oven until they’re nice and golden.

review.reviewBody: These potatoes are fantastic! Since I was preparing a large meal I got a head start on these early in the day by cutting the potatoes and soaking them in water. This will firstly prevent them from discoloration but will also rid the potatoes of excess starch so they roast up crispy on the outside and tender on the inside. To save my sanity cleaning the baking sheet, I first placed a layer of parchment paper down - cleanup's a snap. The best part of these potatoes was by far the parmesan. The potatoes were evenly coated and melted during roasting to form a crunchy, flavorful crust. My kids loved these! Definitely a keeper. Thanks for the recipe!!

Finally made this recipe--I shouldn't have waited so long to try it!! These potatoes are beyond fantastic!!! I could have made a whole meal of them....savory, flavorful,just delicious. I used 6 large baking potatoes to about double the recipe because I wanted some leftovers--well, there weren't any!! I sliced the potatoes in thick slices rather than chunk them, and I didn't double the other ingredients--only increased the parmesan to 3/4 cup. (I think for me it would have been too oily and too much salt if I had doubled everything) I did sprinkle some cheese over the top before I baked them in a roasting pan lined with heavy duty foil at 425 degrees, and it browned wonderfully, with crispy edges to the potatoes. Next time I'm going to have to quadruple it because everyone just went gaga over them. FIVE BIG STARS!!!

Great, Easy Sidedish. I used baby Yukon Gold Potatoes unpeeled. I added 1/2 teaspoon of dried rosemary and upped the thyme to 1/2 teaspoon too. I cut each baby potatoe into six wedges and placed them on parchment paper on a baking sheet. They cooked in 30 minutes at 400 degrees (flipped after 15 minutes) and cleanup was a snap with just tossing the parchment paper. This recipe is much better than any fried potatoes I have had. Served with sour cream and they were a welcome change from ketchup.
I did soak cut potatoes in cold water for half an hour and dried in clean kitchen towels. Added a little garlic and parsley from the garden. If you love potatoes.. this is great!

Easy and delicious. I added some red pepper flakes to give it some pizazz. Next time I'll try cutting the potatoes more like in the pictures. I like the idea of a little garlic powder too, so I'll try that next time. Update: I made it again, using duck fat instead of olive oil, and added garlic powder and dried basil. I find that 400ºF for an hour is too much, so I went with 375ºF for 35 minutes, and broiled for the last 5 minutes. It was delicious, according to my most ardent critic (wife).

Delicious! I used RED potatoes, and tossed in 1 tablespoon of garlic powder and 1 tablespoon of onion powder in the bowl with the olive oil, salt & pepper (no thyme). Only took 25-30 minutes at 400 degrees (never turned 'em). Made this three times to compliment different style of eggs (scrambled, boiled, etc.)..came out beautifully every time. Thank you Kristen!

I followed VRcook's advice and soaked the sliced potatoes earlier in the day. I prepared the recipe as directed and added 1/8 t rosemary and a shake of garlic powder. I also baked with foil for 50 minutes, without foil for 10 minutes, then broiled for a couple minutes to crisp the top. The potatoes baked up perfectly. Flavor was full and savory -- perfect blend of parmesan and herbs. My family devoured them!

Excellent side dish! I used red skinned potatoes and added a bit of rosemary to the mix as it pairs well with thyme. I did bake this at 425 and tossed them once during cooking. They took about 45-50 minutes. They came out crispy and delicious - perfect with grilled steak!

Very simple and so delicious! I cut my red potatoes into bite-size cubes to decrease the cooking time and used the convection roast setting. I prepared it ahead of time and reheated in the microwave. This will be a regular addition to our weekly meals - my family loves red potatoes.

Made this last night and just loved it. Will try with other herbs too. Totally simple and since I cut the potatoes a bit thinner, took only 40 minutes in the oven. Definitely adding this to my repertoire! I left out the salt, the Parmesan seemed salty enough. Great recipe.

Wow!!! made this last night on the barbeques. All I had on hand was mini potatoes, so I cut those in half tossed them in the oil mixture added some rosemary as suggested by others too. I sprayed barbeque foil with Pam, dumped the potatoes on then sprinkled the Parmesan over top!! Cooked on indirect heat for 1 hour. DELISH!
best tasting potatoes my family has had! crispy too
I made it, but I used the little potatoes I had on handand may have cooked it too long. will try again with regular size potatoes
I should have sprayed the pan. The potatoes stuck to the dish.
Very tasty!
Where in the recipe does it list rosemary? Or maybe I'm blind lol!
Make this as written and you can’t go wrong. Don’t skip the thyme; it gives it another layer of flavor.
Amazing! Potatoes were super quick and easy and tasted great! This is my new favorite roasted potatoes recipe!
Add tsp garlic, doubled fresh rosemary. My, this was good.
Don't forget to prepare a bowl cold water and 1/4 cup baking soda, wash and scrub the potatoes' skin first for maximum enjoyment. 😉
